title: Driftward Plateau
description: An asymmetric faulted limestone island with a long keel, detached fragments and a grass-capped summit. The keel starts near Z=0.

review.notes: Round 1 (new build). Big step up from the old island: asymmetric, clearly tapered underside, ledges, a summit with trees, bushes and rocks, floating fragments, and the figure is readable on top. Defects: (1) form_detail: the whole cliff is one uniform layer of lumpy noise displacement (closeup_base reads like melted wax or a brain), with no hard rock strata, flat bedding planes or sharp fracture faces; build 3-5 thick, distinct horizontal strata with crisp overhanging lips and a few vertical faults, and keep the noise only as secondary detail. (2) material: the grass top in closeup.jpg is a blurry, smeared low-resolution texture with large grey blotches, and the cliffs get bluish-grey camouflage mottling in the cooler turns; use the library grass_ground/rock materials at metre-scale coordinates and vary the rock by stratum (lighter caps, darker damp undersides). (3) style/defects: no soil or root layer at the rim, so the grass ends in a knife-cut edge over the cliff; add a 1-3 m dark soil band with roots and grass tufts hanging over the edge. The trees sit in a thin line along the back edge; group them in 2-3 clumps with air between, per STYLE.md. The floating fragments are lumpy potatoes; give them the same strata as the main body, with grass or soil tops on the larger ones.
